From 5f5fa4cd35f707344f65ce9e225b6528691dbbaa Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 15:03:27 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] Bluetooth: MGMT: Fix dangling pointer on
 mgmt_add_adv_patterns_monitor_complete

This fixes the condition checking so mgmt_pending_valid is executed
whenever status != -ECANCELED otherwise calling mgmt_pending_free(cmd)
would kfree(cmd) without unlinking it from the list first, leaving a
dangling pointer. Any subsequent list traversal (e.g.,
mgmt_pending_foreach during __mgmt_power_off, or another
mgmt_pending_valid call) would dereference freed memory.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-bluetooth/20260315132013.75ab40c5@kernel.org/T/#m1418f9c82eeff8510c1beaa21cf53af20db96c06
Fixes: 302a1f674c00 ("Bluetooth: MGMT: Fix possible UAFs")
Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Paul Menzel <pmenzel@molgen.mpg.de>

diff --git a/net/bluetooth/mgmt.c b/net/bluetooth/mgmt.c
index d52238ce6a9a..e5f9287fb826 100644
--- a/net/bluetooth/mgmt.c
+++ b/net/bluetooth/mgmt.c
@@ -5355,7 +5355,7 @@ static void mgmt_add_adv_patterns_monitor_complete(struct hci_dev *hdev,
 	 * hci_adv_monitors_clear is about to be called which will take care of
 	 * freeing the adv_monitor instances.
 	 */
-	if (status == -ECANCELED && !mgmt_pending_valid(hdev, cmd))
+	if (status == -ECANCELED || !mgmt_pending_valid(hdev, cmd))
 		return;
 
 	monitor = cmd->user_data;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies a single file, `net/bluetooth/mgmt.c`, to fix a dangling pointer bug caused by incorrect conditional logic when handling the completion of adding an advertising patterns monitor.

**Modifications in net/bluetooth/mgmt.c**:
- **Changed** the condition in function `mgmt_add_adv_patterns_monitor_complete` from:
  ```c
  if (status == -ECANCELED && !mgmt_pending_valid(hdev, cmd))
  ```
  to:
  ```c
  if (status == -ECANCELED || !mgmt_pending_valid(hdev, cmd))
  ```
  (i.e., replaced logical AND (`&&`) with logical OR (`||`)).

**Relationship**:
The original condition used `&&`, meaning the early return (and thus skipping of `mgmt_pending_free`) occurred only when both conditions were true: status is `-ECANCELED` AND the command is no longer valid. In all other cases (e.g., status is `-ECANCELED` but the command is still valid), the code would proceed to call `mgmt_pending_free(cmd)`, which freed the command memory without first unlinking it from the pending list. This left a dangling pointer, causing use-after-free on subsequent list traversals.

The fix changes the logic to `||`, so that if either condition is true – the status is `-ECANCELED` (cleanup handled elsewhere) OR the command is no longer valid – the function returns immediately without performing any freeing operations. This ensures `mgmt_pending_free` is only reached when status is not `-ECANCELED` and the command is still valid, preventing the double-free/unlink mismatch.

Root cause:
The original condition used logical AND (`&&`) instead of OR (`||`), causing the early return to be skipped when `status == -ECANCELED` and the command was still valid. In that case, `mgmt_pending_free(cmd)` was called without first unlinking the command from the pending list, leading to a dangling pointer and subsequent use-after-free.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
if (status == -ECANCELED && !mgmt_pending_valid(hdev, cmd))
    return;
Reason:
The condition uses logical AND (`&&`), so it only returns early when both `status == -ECANCELED` and `cmd` is not valid. When `status == -ECANCELED` but `cmd` is still valid (i.e., still linked in the pending list), the return is skipped. The code then proceeds to call `mgmt_pending_free(cmd)`, which frees `cmd` without unlinking it from the list, leaving a dangling pointer. Subsequent list traversals (e.g., `mgmt_pending_foreach`) dereference freed memory, causing a use-after-free.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (status == -ECANCELED || !mgmt_pending_valid(hdev, cmd))
    return;
Reason:
The condition is changed to use logical OR (`||`), so the function returns early if either `status == -ECANCELED` (operation cancelled, cleanup will be handled elsewhere) or `cmd` is not valid (already removed from the list). This prevents the subsequent code from calling `mgmt_pending_free(cmd)` on a command that is still linked in the pending list, eliminating the dangling pointer and potential use-after-free.
